title: Contextual recommendation cards for caching & batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Design a compact, scannable card UI in the Redwood Console that surfaces contextual, explainable recommendations for caching and batching configuration. Each card should explain why the change is suggested, estimated impact on latency and cost, safety/guardrails, and provide a one-click 'simulate' and 'apply' flow. The aim is to increase adoption of recommended optimizations while preventing accidental user regressions.

Problem statement: Customers frequently ask for prescriptive guidance on how to lower token cost or reduce tail latency. Existing recommendation views are either too verbose (long text docs) or too technical (CLI examples). We need an in-console affordance that: 1) ties a recommendation to observable signals (recent latency spikes, token mix, model variant), 2) quantifies expected impact and confidence, and 3) makes it easy to try without committing (simulation/sandbox).

Design goals:
- Immediate scanability: cards should fit in a compact list with a concise headline, three key metrics, and an icon for type (batching/caching/quantization).
- Explainability: each card must include a short rationale (2-3 sentences) and a link to a deeper explain panel for engineers who want full traces/benchmarks.
- Safety & guardrails: recommendations that change correctness-sensitive settings (e.g., kv cache TTLs, prefix caching for chat) must show a risk badge and require an explicit confirmation with a rollback window.
- Progressive disclosure & simulation: primary CTA is 'Simulate' which runs an offline cost/latency estimate and shows a diff of historical requests if possible. Secondary CTA is 'Apply' with canary/rollout options.
- Traceability & audit: each card should include a reference id that maps to the Recommendation Engine (for ops/incident correlation) and an immutable changelog entry when applied.

Proposed card anatomy (top-to-bottom):
1) Headline: short action e.g., 'Increase batching window to 50ms for route /chat/stream'
2) Badges: type (Batching), confidence (High/Medium/Low), risk (None/Low/High)
3) Key metrics row: estimated latency delta, estimated cost delta, expected throughput gain (icons + numbers)
4) Rationale: 1–2 sentence reason with signal anchors (e.g., "95th latency > 600ms on 2025-02-05; small batch sizes observed")
5) Controls: [Simulate] [Apply ▶] overflow menu (Apply with rollout, Create ticket, Dismiss for 7d)
6) Secondary link: 'View evidence & benchmarks' opens right panel with traces, sample requests, and recommended rollout policy (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

States to cover in prototype:
- Empty state: no recommendations; show proactive CTAs to run a diagnostics job and link to docs.
- Loading state: skeleton card with metric placeholders.
- Simulation result state: show simulated cost/latency curves, highlight percentiles affected, and a 'confidence breakdown' list.
- Applied state: card becomes collapsed with 'Applied on <date> — rollout 10% -> 100% scheduled', and actions to rollback.
- Rejected/dismissed: allow users to snooze a card and capture reason (false positive, risk too high, not relevant).

Accessibility considerations:
- Ensure cards are navigable via keyboard; primary CTAs first in tab order.
- Use color + icon + text for badges so status remains visible to color-blind users.
- Provide aria-live regions for simulation results and apply confirmations.

Prototype assets & links:
- Figma file (working prototype): https://redwood.figshare.com/console-recs/cards-2025
- Annotated evidence example (Drive): https://drive.redwood/inference/recs/example-evidence-2025.pdf
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CONSOLE/Recommendation+Cards+Spec

Open questions for PM/Eng:
- Which engine signals are guaranteed available in-console (we currently have latency histograms and token size distribution; per-request KV hit rates are partial)?
- What is the canonical id to map a recommendation back to Recommendation Engine outputs? (Ops needs stable mapping for rollback tracing).
- Should simulation run against live traffic (shadow) or historical sampling only? (Security and privacy constraints may apply).

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity prototype exists in Figma covering all states and interactions.
- Usability study (n=6 engineers/PMs) completed with summary notes and at least one iteration.
- Engineering acceptance: ENG owner confirms feasibility for simulate endpoints and apply rollout API.
- Console e2e checklist updated with audit log requirement and rollback UX.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Engineers may over-apply recommendations that affect correctness. Mitigation: explicit risk badge, require manual confirmation and create an automatic rollback window by default.
- Risk: Simulation mismatches reality. Mitigation: show confidence bands and clearly label assumptions (dataset window used, model variant).

Next steps:
1) Finalize UX copy with content designer (Due: 2025-02-14).
2) Run quick hallway usability tests and incorporate feedback (Due: 2025-02-17).
3) Handoff to ENG for API contract (Due: 2025-02-20).
